verified: S1: before dumping old bytes, each replacement target is debugfs-stat'ed and must be 'Type: regular' with parsable Mode, User/Group and Links == 1; otherwise it is refused before any mutation. The old mode, uid and gid are recorded as replaces_metadata and reapplied after write: mode as 0100000|mode, plus uid and gid. The recorded executable flag is derived from the old mode, not the caller's hint. New (non-replacement) files keep the mode-from-hint with explicit uid/gid 0.

S2: run() flushes the Python log before every child. The batch output offset is taken after a flush (tell() reaches the raw lseek). After debugfs the batch slice is parsed: the 'debugfs: ' echoes must equal the command list exactly and in order, 'Allocated inode: N' must appear exactly once per written file, and any other non-blank line (except the 'debugfs ' version header) refuses with the failure log preserved. A 'debugfs:'-prefixed error line is also caught, because it would break the exact echo sequence. stderr is merged, so com_err lines such as 'write: ...' are seen.
Unchanged: baseline hash gate, private copy, old-bytes hash check before rm, the parent-directory stat fix, dump-back sha256, final e2fsck -fn, exclusive os.link publication, 0444 image.

That log shows 'write: Ext2 file already exists' caught by S2, where dump-back would have matched because the bytes were identical. Wrong old hash refused, as before.

notes.text: batch_lines decodes the slice as strict UTF-8. Non-UTF-8 debugfs output would raise UnicodeDecodeError before preserve_failure(), so it still fails closed but without the failure log. Suggest decode('utf-8', 'replace').

The header exemption accepts any line starting with 'debugfs ' (space). Matching the exact version banner (for example ^debugfs \d+\.\d+(\.\d+)? \() would remove the only remaining unchecked prefix. In practice debugfs errors are prefixed with the command name or 'debugfs:', so both are caught today.
